label: Closed-collection rootedness: positive arguments, rivals and provisional judgment
summary: Analyst warrant assessment; no source was read, and every literature name below is an unread lead from memory, not an attribution. Meaning (DEF closed-collection rootedness): collect actual concreta together with everything that actually gives being to any of them; the collection contains something to which no actual concretum gives being. It forbids only rootless closed collections: a pure endless descent and a pure cycle. It allows endless descent and cycles above a root, and imposes no asymmetry, transitivity or finite-path condition. Positive arguments. (A) Dependence transmission ('borrowed reality'): in a rootless closed collection each member has being only as supplied by members, and nothing in the collection has being otherwise; the argument's claim is that wholly supplied being needs a supplier that is not itself supplied. Formally this claim is CCR itself, so it adds no derivation; its content is the intuition, and its strength is that it is about the collection, not about the length of chains. It does not support AGWF over CCR: a limit root that grounds every member of a descending chain (Cameron-style foundation reached through infinitely many intermediaries, an unread lead from #310) satisfies it. (B) Per se attenuation (closedRootedOfAttenuation): valid, and it can fail: its load-bearing clauses are uniform loss and a common bound, and the existing controls show each is needed (binaryFixed, halfFixed). The per se clause, own esse only at roots (intermediates contribute nothing of their own), is the traditional one; the uniform-loss clause is not: no independent justification is on file for the claim that instrumental transmission of being loses a fixed fraction, and the traditional instrument examples are not described as lossy. So 'intermediates have no power of their own' alone does not yield CCR: lossless per se reception is satisfied by the pure regress, which violates CCR. (C) Graded argument: the limit grounder satisfies ascent along a grade with a maximum while the grade has infinite ascent; with #1515's equivalence this shows grades supply no independent warrant for no infinite ascent, and none for CCR was found. Rivals (objection standard). R1 grounding infinitism (leads: Bohn, Morganti, Bliss, Schaffer 2003, Tahko; unread). Target: CCR (formal shape Control.pureRegress). Mechanism: an actual rootless closed collection, each member grounded by another, the totality accounted for memberwise or holistically. Independent justification offered: the conceivability or physical possibility of no fundamental level, mostly compositional (gunk). Relevance: only if the selected relation (present esse support, principal sustaining) is read as compositional dependence of wholes on parts, or if a positive account of source-free real sustaining is given (#310: a coinductive or global fixed-point reading); the possibility arguments concern possibility, CCR the actual world. Price: an actual collection whose being is supplied by nothing outside it, with no member having being otherwise. Status: the strongest standing rival; not refuted; no established counterexample. R2 coherentism or symmetric dependence (leads: Thompson 2016, Barnes 2018, Swanson; unread). Against CCR only for pure cycles; rooted cycles satisfy CCR (Control.rootedCycle), so against the join the rival must claim a pure cycle of sustaining with nothing outside it. Its recalled examples concern identity or nature dependence of relational items, not sustaining of concrete existence; it remains a substantive objection to asymmetry and to J2 (both still needed off the join's coverage routes). R3 infinite descending chains with a limit grounder: not a rival to CCR, a model of it; a rival only to AGWF and to no infinite ascent, and the coverage routes now accommodate it. R4 unbounded ascent: as recorded for the graded batch, it targets only the global no-infinite-ascent premise. Overall provisional judgment (revisable; not establishment): the join's regress commitment is strictly lowered from AGWF to CCR, which keeps the motivations offered for AGWF (borrowed being needs an unborrowed giver; foundation as common ultimate basis) while dropping their unmotivated surplus (no infinite chains, no cycles above a root). Support for the join's regress step is therefore modestly higher than under AGWF: the foundation-friendly regress views are compatible with it, and only pure infinitism and pure coherentism remain as rivals, each carrying the price of a sourceless closed collection of actual sustained beings. Positive warrant for CCR rests mainly on (A); (B) adds little until uniform loss is independently motivated. Neither rival is refuted.
blocker: Revision conditions: an account on which the selected sustaining relation is compositional over actual gunky parts; a defended source-free global fixed-point account of real sustaining (#310 ACT-GROUND); an independent motivation for uniform attenuation of received being (would upgrade B); an established pure cycle of existential sustaining. Next tests: read one infinitist source (Morganti or Bohn) and Cameron 2008 sections 1 and 4-6 before citing them; test whether a weaker per se clause (things with partly own esse) still gives CCR; investigate a collection-level warrant for CCR that does not reduce to it (for example a PSR for closed collections, #312).
